items.title: Computer Vision and Voice-Based AI Technologies for Assistive Systems
items.abstract: Assistive technologies increasingly apply artificial intelligence to support access to physical environments, visual information, communication, and human-computer interaction. This review synthesizes eight selected studies covering indoor navigation, interactive object search, Indian Sign Language recognition, gesture-to-text interaction, real-time hand tracking, vision-language navigation, multilingual assistance, and wake-word detection. The studies are organized into two broad themes: computer vision-based assistance and voice-based AI. A narrative comparison examines the tasks addressed, technical approaches, input and output modalities, evaluation designs, reported findings, and limitations. The literature illustrates a movement from infrastructure-assisted guidance and constrained recognition toward open-vocabulary object search and vision-language interaction, while also showing the continuing importance of efficient perception and speech-activation components. The reviewed studies use heterogeneous evidence, including small user studies, image-classification experiments, device-level measurements, surveys, and prototype demonstrations; their results therefore should not be ranked through one common accuracy score. Recurring needs include broader real-world validation, generalization across users and environments, sustained contextual interaction, accessible user feedback, efficient deployment, and more consistent evaluation reporting. This paper is a synthesis of existing published work and does not propose a new system or report project-specific experiments. Keywords: Assistive Technology; Computer Vision; Voice-Based AI; Accessibility; Human-Computer Interaction; Multimodal AI

items.title: Consumer Responses to AI-Generated Marketing Content: Evidence from an Experimental Survey
items.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for digital marketing, particularly in short video advertising. However, consumer acceptance of AI-generated advertisements remains uncertain because of the concerns over authenticity, trust and emotional connection. This study investigates how consumers respond to short video advertisements created by AI and humans through comparing evaluations and identifying factors that influence engagement intention and purchase intention. A quantitative survey was conducted with 179 participants, where respondents evaluated both advertisement formats. Reliability analysis, multiple linear regression models, paired samples t-tests, and qualitative analysis of open-ended responses were applied. The results show that human-created advertisements received much higher evaluations in authenticity, trust, visual appeal, professionalism, engagement intention, and purchase intention, while informativeness showed no significant difference. Regression results further indicate that trust is the strongest factor influencing consumer responses towards AI-generated advertisements. These findings indicate that businesses should balance AI efficiency and human creativity to improve consumer acceptance and advertising effectiveness.

items.title: Continuous monitoring biosensors for advanced healthcare and environmental applications: challenges, material innovations and future directions
items.abstract: This review critically discusses the development of continuous monitoring biosensors and the technological developments that have facilitated the transition from one-off or periodic measurement sensors to longer-term, connected and autonomous sensors. One hundred forty-four publications were analysed using a bibliometric approach, giving a map of the field that illustrates its growth, multidisciplinary aspects, technological development and key application areas. Electrochemical and optical transduction strategies are discussed in a systematic manner along with the advanced functional materials such as carbon nanotubes, graphene quantum dots, MXenes, covalent organic frameworks, molecularly imprinted polymers, functional polymers, hydrogels and chiral composites. Specific focus is placed on the use of these materials as an enhancement of charge transfer, analyte accessibility, selectivity, reversible recognition, antifouling behaviour, mechanical flexibility, signal stability and sensor regeneration. Architectures for wearable, implantable, biodegradable and self-powered are presented for continuous monitoring of clinically relevant biomarkers and metabolites, and platforms for environmental monitoring of waterborne pollutants, heavy metals and antibiotics, pathogens and other contaminants are explored. The review also examines the incorporation of microfluidics, wireless communication, artificial intelligence/machine learning, edge and cloud computing and Internet of Things technologies, which show the evolution towards multiplexed, connected and closed-loop biosensing systems. In all of these areas, analysis reveals that barriers to translation include sensor regeneration, biofouling, signal drift, matrix interference, calibration, energy requirements, biocompatibility, device integration, scalability, cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and limited clinical/field validation. Notably, analytical parameters, including sensitivity and limit of detection, are demonstrated to be inadequate to assess deployment readiness, and long-term stability, matrix tolerance, reproducibility and real-world validation are all required. The areas identified for future direction include regenerative and antifouling sensing interfaces, multimodal and self-powered platforms, physiomimetic and minimally invasive architectures, AI-enabled signal interpretation, standardized performance metrics, scalable manufacturing, and rigorous clinical and environmental validation. In general, the review highlights advanced materials, biorecognition, device engineering, energy management, digital connectivity, and data analytics as the critical enabler for reliable continuous biosensing for personalized healthcare and environmental monitoring applications.

items.title: Control Room Alarm Management and Human Factors in Large Liquefied Natural Gas Facilities: A Comprehensive Review of Rationalization Frameworks, Operator Response, and the Elimination of Standing and Inhibited Alarms
items.abstract: The alarm system is the principal channel through which a liquefaction plant informs its control room operators that the process has departed from its intended envelope, and it is among the least reliably managed protective layers in the modern process facility. This review synthesises four literatures that bear on the problem and are rarely brought together: the standards and guidance architecture specifying what an alarm system must do; the control engineering research that has characterised the mechanisms of alarm overloading and developed quantitative methods for addressing them; the human factors and applied psychology research on how operators actually respond to annunciation, including the substantial body of work on alarm mistrust and the crywolf effect; and the incident investigation record, which supplies the consequences. Six findings organise the review. First, the performance benchmarks published in the principal standards are attainable in continuous liquefaction service but are attained by a minority of installations, and the gap is a design and governance gap rather than a technology gap. Second, the dominant contributors to alarm overloading are structural rather than incidental, comprising chattering annunciation, configuration that ignores operating state, alarms designed in isolation from related variables, and the propagation of a single abnormality through physically connected units. Third, standing alarms and inhibited alarms are distinct failure modes with distinct causes, and treating them as one backlog is the most common reason rationalization programmes stall. Fourth, operator response to annunciation is a calibrated response to observed system reliability rather than a training deficiency, which means alarm quality is a determinant of response behaviour and not a housekeeping matter. Fifth, every metric in the standard performance set can be improved without improving the alarm system, so reporting arrangements require paired measures. Sixth, the features of the liquefaction context, multi-train configuration with shared utilities and flare headers, long thermal transients and cryogenic inventory, qualify the general guidance in ways that have received almost no published treatment.

items.title: Conventional to advanced techniques: Progress in titanium alloys for biomedical applications
items.abstract: The biocompatibility, high strength-to-weight ratio, mechanical properties, and resistance to corrosion of titanium and its alloys, making them suitable for implants. The major factors influencing titanium implant performance depends on fabrication technique, microstruc­ture, resistance to corrosion, tribocorrosion, osseointegration and its stability. This review focuses the impact of conventional manufacturing technique such as welding, casting, powder metallurgy, forging, rolling, and extrusion and their effect on metal implants. To overcome the limitations of conventional techniques, further development of advanced manufacturing strategies capable of achieving complex geometries and tailored properties for next-generation biomedical implants. Specific focus is placed on powder bed fusion, directed energy deposition, material extrusion, binder jetting, and material jetting. The impact of processing technique on mechanical properties, microstructure, corrosion resistance and overall implant longevity is discussed. Furthermore, challenges such as the high elastic modulus of conventional Ti alloys, limited control over the strength, ductility, biocompatibility, surface degradation and tribocorrosion, and the need for adaptive and long-term implant monitoring continue to drive research toward integrated material, computational, manufacturing, and digital strategies. Emerging approaches such as high-entropy titanium alloys, artificial intelligence, machine learning, 4D printing, smart implant technologies, and digital twinning for predicting and controlling implant performance, are emphasised in this review. Their incorporation with additive manufacturing (AM) opens new possibilities for enhancing Ti implants, which can offer improved mechanical compatibility, corrosion resistance, wear resistance, personalized functionality, and consistent long-term performance.

items.title: Conversational AI for Perceived Cognitive Decline Screening in Older Adults
items.abstract: Early detection of cognitive decline in older adults remains challenging due to the resource demands of standard neuropsychological assessments. Chatbot-based Intelligent Cognitive Assistants (ICAs) provide a scalable alternative by eliciting open-ended responses rich in linguistic, semantic, and autobiographical cues. This study evaluates whether ICA question-answer (Q/A) interviews with older adults can screen for participant-reported perceived cognitive decline and related cognitive, functional, and personality outcomes. We compare traditional machine learning, frozen transformer embeddings, fine-tuned transformers, and large language model (LLM) reasoning strategies across Global Q/A, Single Q/A confidence averaging, and Aggregated Q/A pipelines. Among text-based methods, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite (1-example-per-class, Aggregated Q/A) achieved the highest held-out test performance (0.742 accuracy, 0.739 balanced accuracy, 0.728 macro-F1). Given the small test set (n = 31), these results are interpreted descriptively. Frozen clinical transformer embeddings with a random forest head led non-LLM text methods, whereas fine-tuned models showed limited generalization. Models utilizing structured questionnaires, cognitive tasks, and personality traits outperformed text-based models in classification. Continuous regression analyses revealed modest predictive signals for AD8, FAQ, IQCODE, neuroticism, and conscientiousness. Exploratory prompt-level analyses identified both direct symptom-related and indirect autobiographical questions with strong test metrics, though sample sizes varied across prompts. These findings indicate that ICA chatbot interviews capture meaningful signals of perceived cognitive decline, supporting scalable screening research. Larger, clinically diverse cohorts with validated clinical outcomes are needed for clinical translation.

items.title: Corporate Accountability by Algorithm: AI and the Interpretation of Human Rights Due Diligence
items.abstract: Abstract As companies struggle to conduct human rights due diligence and governments attempt to monitor compliance with supply chain regulations, they are increasingly turning to digital technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI). While AI-based tools can improve supply chain visibility and assess human rights risks, they carry potential risks of marginalizing rightsholders and undermining traditional conceptions of corporate accountability. This article examines the methodologies behind these tools, the role of technology firms in their design and application and the unintended consequences of relying on those firms to interpret the legal norm of human rights due diligence. It draws on a critical analysis of AI-based tools as well as interviews with officials from technology firms, consultants and human rights advocates. I argue that although AI can enhance human rights due diligence, AI-driven corporate accountability delegates interpretive judgment to technology firms, privatizes human rights and deemphasizes stakeholder engagement.

items.title: Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization
items.abstract: Self-distillation policy optimization provides dense token-level supervision for LLM post-training through feedback-conditioned self-teachers. However, directly matching the self-teacher can disrupt successful behaviors on correct rollouts while providing insufficient correction on incorrect ones. We propose Asymmetric Policy Optimization via Self-Distillation (APSD), which constructs correctness-dependent targets by mixing student and self-teacher distributions: interpolation preserves successful behaviors on correct rollouts, while extrapolation beyond the self-teacher strengthens correction on incorrect ones. We analyze APSD through divergence decomposition, reverse-KL barycentric geometry, and gradient analysis, highlighting the importance of gradient flow through student-dependent targets. Experiments under reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards and rich feedback show that APSD achieves strong overall performance against reinforcement-learning and self-distillation baselines and matches SDPO performance with 2.6x fewer training steps on average across Qwen3 model scales.

items.title: Cost-aware evaluation of time-series foundation models for urban air-quality and temperature forecasting
items.abstract: Cities with the greatest need for hyper-local air-quality and weather forecasts often have the shortest data records and the tightest compute budgets. The usual responses, searching for a tiny architecture or transferring from data-rich cities, assume foundation models are too heavy, an assumption more often adopted than tested. Across 29 cities and two domains (hourly PM2.5 and 2 m temperature), under pre-specified protocols with measured energy and a cost-adjusted decision rule, we compare all three. On PM2.5 three zero-shot foundation models spanning two families and a 4.3-fold size range are statistically indistinguishable from the tuned specialist in mean absolute scaled error (MASE 0.659-0.662 vs. 0.692 under deployable causal covariates) and formally equivalent to one another. The specialist’s apparent temperature edge (0.533 vs. 0.792) depends heavily on covariate timing: 0.638 with covariates carrying measured 24-h forecast error, 0.745 with only values knowable at the forecast origin. Perfect foresight therefore distorts the cross-domain comparison, as it can in any benchmark using future covariates. Transfer learning never significantly beats zero-shot at any budget. Under frequent retraining the untrained model uses roughly ten times less measured energy, though a once-trained specialist eventually amortizes. Where models are refreshed often, downloading one now matches training one.

items.title: Creative constants in architectural education: augmenting the use of keywords through innovative practices
items.abstract: This paper examines the potential of keywords, understood as creative constants, as pedagogical tools to stimulate creativity in the early stages of architectural study. Rather than equating words with experiences, keywords are framed as catalysts enabling incremental and iterative design concept generation. The study situates this approach within recent developments in Artificial Intelligence, which introduce new paradigms for understanding creativity in design education. The methodology combines the analysis of theoretical precedents, such as the use of images and narratives in literature, with practical experimentation through analogue studio exercises and AI-assisted text-to-image platforms. This dual approach demonstrates how keywords can help students bridge abstract ideas and design action while accelerating iterative exploration. Developed through a multidisciplinary perspective, the research connects insights from literature, design theory, pedagogy, and emerging digital tools. The findings suggest that keywords support students in constructing a personal repertoire of creative constants applicable across different stages of the design process. By integrating analogue and AI-supported methods, the paper proposes a pedagogical framework to nurture creativity and innovation in architectural education.

items.title: Critical Success Factors for AI Training Robot Adoption in Accounting SMEs: An Integrated Delphi–DEMATEL–ANP Approach
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Robotic Process Automation (RPA) are transforming accounting services toward intelligent, data-driven professional services. However, small and medium-sized accounting firms (SMEs) face barriers to AI adoption, including limited resources, technological capabilities, employee skills, and regulatory uncertainty. This study identifies and prioritizes the critical success factors (CSFs) influencing AI training robot adoption in Taiwanese accounting SMEs. The framework integrates the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework, Task–Technology Fit (TTF), Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Human–Computer Trust (HCT), and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI). We used a two-round Delphi process with 15 experts to refine the CSFs, followed by DEMATEL to identify causal relationships and ANP to assess their relative priorities. The DEMATEL results indicate that the Technological dimension is the strongest causal driver (D−R = 1.355), followed by the Organizational dimension (D−R = 0.435), whereas Decision Making is the principal effect dimension (D−R = −1.781). The findings further emphasize task–technology alignment, AI maturity, regulatory conditions, top management support, employee AI competence, and human–computer trust. Overall, AI adoption represents an integrated organizational transformation rather than merely a technological investment. The proposed Delphi–DEMATEL–ANP framework provides systematic decision support for resource prioritization, organizational readiness, capability development, and sustainable AI-enabled digital transformation in accounting SMEs. items.title: Cross-Dataset Generalization of Deep Learning for Retinal Vessel Segmentation in Fundus Images: External Evaluation from DRIVE to CHASE_DB1
items.abstract: Automated retinal vessel segmentation can support quantitative analysis of fundus photographs and facilitate measurement of vascular characteristics associated with ocular and systemic disease. Although deep-learning methods achieve high segmentation performance on benchmark datasets, their reliability may decrease when applied to images obtained under different acquisition conditions. This study evaluated the cross-dataset generalizability of a U-Net segmentation architecture incorporating an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet34 encoder. Sixteen images from the DRIVE dataset were used for model training and four were retained for in-domain validation. Images were resized to 256 × 256 pixels and processed using a consistent normalization pipeline, while spatial and photometric augmentation was applied during training. Without target-domain retraining or domain adaptation, the trained model was subsequently evaluated on the independent CHASE_DB1 dataset. Segmentation performance was assessed using the Dice coefficient, intersection over union (IoU), and sensitivity, together with qualitative examination of predicted vessel maps. On the held-out DRIVE images, the model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.7263, IoU of 0.5703, and sensitivity of 0.7201. On CHASE_DB1, performance decreased to 0.6269, 0.4573, and 0.5502, respectively. The disproportionately larger reduction in sensitivity indicated an increased frequency of missed vessel pixels under cross-dataset evaluation. Qualitative examination showed greater fragmentation and omission of fine and peripheral vascular structures in CHASE_DB1 images. These findings demonstrate that within-dataset performance may overestimate the robustness of retinal vessel segmentation models when transferred to a different imaging domain. External evaluation should therefore form an important component of retinal imaging artificial intelligence research. Future work should investigate higher-resolution processing, vessel-width-specific evaluation, multi-domain training, domain-adaptation strategies, and larger multicentre datasets to improve model generalizability.

items.title: Curriculum Learning Teaches LLMs Long-Horizon Implicit Reasoning, Up To A Limit
items.abstract: LLMs "reason" by externalizing intermediate steps as tokens through chain-of-thought (CoT), yet even frontier reasoning models hit abrupt performance cliffs on long-horizon tasks. Implicit reasoning (reasoning within a single forward pass) is useful during CoT generation, as the model can "search ahead" to decide the correct next move without explicit search. Models with weak implicit reasoning are more likely to commit to wrong paths and must attempt to recover via backtracking, while models with strong implicit reasoning identify the correct proof strategy directly, shortening the CoT. However, prior work shows LLMs struggle to reason implicitly beyond shallow depths, with no relief from scale. We investigate whether curriculum learning can extend this depth by fine-tuning on examples with progressively increasing vocabulary size and lookahead (the number of steps a model must search ahead to identify the correct next move). At matched compute, curriculum-trained models achieve lookaheads where no-curriculum training fails. Qwen3-0.6B reaches 98% accuracy on problems with lookahead up to 256 with curriculum, compared to 45% without. However, progress slows as fine-tuning continues, following a saturating exponential that suggests a maximum intrinsic lookahead to which models can learn to reason implicitly. Larger models reach higher fitted ceilings, fine-tuning pretrained models far outpaces training from scratch, and curriculum step sizes that are too large stall progression. Finally, the capability acquired on synthetic data transfers to natural language reasoning, with curriculum-trained models outperforming models trained without curriculum at matched compute on 11 natural language reasoning benchmarks.

items.title: Dampak Konten Berbasis Artificial Intelligence terhadap Literasi Digital Generasi Alpha: A Structured Literature Review
items.abstract: Abstrak: Perkembangan generative AI telah mengubah ekosistem informasi digital secara masif, namun kebijakan literasi yang menyasar Generasi Alpha sebagai konsumen utama konten sintetis masih sangat terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis tren konten berbasis AI yang dikonsumsi generasi muda, mengidentifikasi dampaknya terhadap literasi digital Generasi Alpha, serta merumuskan strategi mitigasi untuk memperkuat kemampuan kritis generasi tersebut. Metode yang digunakan adalah Structured Literature Review (SLR) dengan protokol PRISMA, melibatkan 15 artikel ilmiah terindeks yang dipublikasikan pada rentang 2021–2025 dan diseleksi melalui kriteria inklusi dan eksklusi yang ketat. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa tren konten berbasis AI berkembang pesat di level pendidikan tinggi namun belum proporsional pada level pendidikan dasar. Dampak konten AI bersifat kondisional: positif dalam setting pembelajaran terstruktur, namun berpotensi memperdalam ketergantungan teknologi dan melemahkan kemampuan evaluasi kritis tanpa pendampingan pedagogis yang memadai. Strategi mitigasi yang efektif mencakup pengembangan kerangka AI literacy pada level individu, penguatan peran institusi pendidikan, dan kebijakan sistemik yang adaptif. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa literasi digital di era AI bukan kompetensi yang berkembang secara alami, melainkan perlu dibangun secara sadar dan terstruktur melalui pendekatan berlapis. Keywords: Literasi digital; Generasi Alpha; konten berbasis AI; generative AI; misinformasi Abstrak: The rapid development of generative AI has fundamentally transformed the digital information ecosystem, yet literacy policies targeting Generation Alpha as primary consumers of synthetic content remain critically limited. This study aims to analyze trends in AI-based content consumed by young people, identify its impacts on Generation Alpha’s digital literacy, and formulate mitigation strategies to strengthen their critical competencies. A Structured Literature Review (SLR) method with PRISMA protocol was employed, involving 15 indexed scientific articles published between 2021 and 2025, selected through rigorous inclusion and exclusion criteria. Findings indicate that AI-based content trends have advanced rapidly at the higher education level but remain disproportionately underaddressed at the primary education level. The impact of AI content is conditional: positive within structured learning environments, yet potentially deepening technological dependency and weakening critical evaluation skills without adequate pedagogical guidance. Effective mitigation strategies encompass the development of AI literacy frameworks at the individual level, strengthening the role of educational institutions, and adaptive systemic policies. This study concludes that digital literacy in the AI era is not a naturally developing competency but must be intentionally and systematically cultivated through a multilayered approach. Keywords: Digital literacy; Generation Alpha; AI-based content; generative AI; misinformation

items.title: Decoding urban thermal well-being: bridging the gap between physical cooling and social perception in wetlands via AI-enhanced sensing
items.abstract: Abstract Urban wetland parks serve as vital infrastructure for climate resilience, yet a critical epistemological gap remains between their objective thermodynamic performance and the subjective thermal well-being of visitors. To bridge this divide, this study establishes an integrated computational social science framework that couples remote sensing metrics with AI-decoded digital narratives. Focusing on the high-density context of Shenzhen, we synthesized Landsat-derived environmental data with large-scale crowd-sourced digital footprints, employing Large Language Models (LLMs) to extract in-situ thermal sentiments from 11,109 online reviews. The analysis suggests that human thermal experience may follow non-linear trajectories relative to physical indicators. Patch Richness Density (PRD) was strongly associated with cooling efficiency, suggesting that landscape heterogeneity may enhance thermal well-being through both physical air exchange and the psychological benefits of visual complexity. The study further identifies a counter-intuitive “accessibility paradox”: a moderate density of impervious-surface patches (PD-I) is associated with higher “cool” perception, with an exploratory empirical turning point around 32.3 n/ha in the Shenzhen wetland-park sample. This pattern suggests that well-distributed access infrastructure may act as a behavioral mediator, facilitating visitor access to cooling cores while remaining subject to site-specific ecological and urban-morphological conditions. Additionally, comfortable perception shows an empirical turning point around a Land Surface Temperature (LST) of 28.8 °C, indicating a context-dependent adaptation range rather than a universal comfort standard. These findings challenge the conventional “minimize-pavement” assumption and suggest that thermal satisfaction depends on a strategic balance between ecological integrity and recreational accessibility. Rather than providing prescriptive design benchmarks, the identified non-linear patterns offer hypothesis-generating evidence and indicative design references for human-centric urban governance. This study contributes a replicable, AI-enhanced paradigm for aligning climate resilience research with public thermal perception.

items.title: Deep learning-based echocardiography for cardiac assessment: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Aims Artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning (DL), has shown significant potential for enhancing the assessment of echocardiograms in clinical practice. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of DL models and to identify factors affecting their performance. Methods and results A systematic review of the PubMed, CENTRAL, and Web of Science databases was conducted, yielding 16 248 potential publications. Of these, 160 studies met the inclusion criteria. Only studies applying fully automated DL networks to echocardiographic loops were considered. Performance estimates were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis. The studies were categorized into five distinct groups: prediction of disease or mortality, replication of established measures, segmentation of cardiac chambers, classification of chamber views, and assessment of image quality. High heterogeneity that could not be resolved was observed in studies focusing on cardiac chamber segmentation and classification. Model performance was influenced by a variety of different factors, including medical target and input characteristics such as video resolution, number of frames used, and total participants included during training. Conclusion DL models achieve high performance across various applications in echocardiography. In selected tasks, they may reduce reliance on expert input and support greater automation of echocardiographic workflows. However, further validation, assessment of clinical utility, and evaluation in real-world settings are required before widespread clinical adoption.

items.title: Deep Learning-Based Multi-Class Cancer Image Classification: A Robust and Explainable Framework
items.abstract: Cancer is still one of the most common causes of death globally, and early and precise detection are crucial for enhancing the survival and treatment of cancer patients.The advent of deep learning has shown great promise for automation in cancer image analysis, but most models are poorly interpretable, widely fail to use global contextual information, and fail to produce the same results across different medical image datasets.The current research presents an Explainable and robust framework for multi-class cancer diagnosis called Deep Learning-Based Multi-Class Cancer Image Classification which integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), feature fusion by attention mechanism, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques for accurate and interpretable cancer diagnosis.This proposed methodology starts from broad-based image preprocessing techniques such as image resizing, image normalization, image contrast enhancement, noise removal, and data augmentation, before conducting parallel feature detection using various CNN and Vision Transformer architectures.An adaptive attention module combines information from local and global feature representations to produce high-level discriminative features, and introducing visual and quantitative explanations for the classification decision, with Grad-CAM and SHAP improves interpretability and trustliness for the medical reader.The proposed framework was tested on publicly available image datasets related to cancer including BreakHis, LC25000, ISIC, PatchCamelyon and TCGA with the same set of experimental conditions, while compared with state-of-the-art deep learning models: VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3, and Vision Transformer.Various performance metrics like Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 score, Specificity, ROC AUC and Confusion Matrix analysis were used in the experimental evaluation.The performance of the proposed framework was outstanding with an overall classification accuracy of 98.46%, precision of 98.29%, recall of 98.11%, F1score of 98.20% and a ROC-AUC of 0.997 which was better than the already existing benchmark machine learning models.The effectiveness of the attention-based feature fusion module was validated by ablation studies, which showed that the combinations of the two architectures CNN and Vision Transformer to be able to improve the feature representation.Moreover, clinically meaningful visual explanations are generated by the Explainable AI, but with no loss of predictive performance.The obtained results show that the proposed approach is powerful, scalable and is very suitable for future clinical cancer diagnosis support systems as well as intelligent computeraided diagnosis.

items.title: Deepfake Detection In Multi-Model Using Deep Learning
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) refers to the broad field where machines are trained to carry out tasks such as learning, reasoning and decision-making.Deep Learning (DL) is a branch of AI that relies on multi-layered neural networks to extract features automatically, handling complex data like images and videos with high accuracy, which makes it well-suited for deepfake detection.Current detection systems mostly depend on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to examine spatial artifacts in video frames, alongside frequency-domain analysis to pick up subtle inconsistencies.While these approaches yield solid results on benchmark datasets and underpin much of the existing detection research, they tend to fall short when dealing with low-quality, compressed or rapidly changing fake videos.To address these limitations, we introduce a multi-modal deep learning framework that combines CNNbased video preprocessing, LSTM temporal analysis and audio feature extraction with ongoing retraining.Together, these elements considerably improve the robustness, adaptability and accuracy of deepfake detection in practical settings, reaching 98.47% accuracy on the FaceForensics++ benchmark.

items.title: Delegating Ourselves Away: Preserve Human Voice and Choice in Next-Generation Digital Systems
items.abstract: Agentic AI is reshaping the framing of equity and inclusion in information systems research. The editorial opens with an urgent call for a conversation about inclusion and equity in the age of agentic AI, given concerns that humans are increasingly removed from knowledge work in human-AI interactions. It then reflects on the digital systems research presented at HICSS over the past 60 years and explains how a new permanent research track has been established to focus on equitable and inclusive digital systems in society and institutions. The editorial outlines what agentic AI is changing, the equity and inclusion risks that follow, and the urgent research agenda this track is uniquely positioned to lead. It ends with a summary of the five papers published in this special issue, which advance our knowledge of equitable and inclusive digital systems from diverse perspectives, and calls for scholars and scientists in the research communities to pay attention to the profound socio-technical paradigm shift driven by the transition from traditional AI to generative AI and to agentic AI.

items.title: Design and Analysis of the Transfer Trajectory for the LUMIO Cislunar CubeSat Mission
items.abstract: Abstract The Earth–Moon system is constantly impacted by Solar System meteoroids causing threats to space and ground assets. A detailed characterization of meteoroid impact magnitudes, velocities, and distribution in time and space is fundamental for a proper space threats assessment and mitigation. The lunar surface is a natural detector of such impact phenomena. The LUMIO CubeSat mission aims to observe and characterize meteoroid impacts on the lunar farside, enhancing lunar situational awareness and complementing Earth-based observations of the lunar near-side. This study presents the mission design and analysis of LUMIO’s transfer trajectory, which exploits weak stability boundary dynamics to achieve a cost-effective insertion into the target halo orbit. Leveraging weak stability boundaries reduces the required spacecraft propellant and increases the number of launch opportunities. While focusing on the specific LUMIO mission, this work also highlights key features of the weak stability boundary transfer design which might prove useful for future cislunar missions, and especially for miniaturized platforms.

items.title: Design and Evaluation of FALL-E: A Robotic Rollator for Studying Balance Response to Overground Perturbation
items.abstract: This paper presents the design and evaluation of a robotic rollator, FALL-E, developed to investigate how individuals respond to perturbations during overground walking with an assistive device. Drawing inspiration from perturbation methods used in treadmill and kinesthetic haptic studies, we introduce a novel overground perturbation technique that delivers brief, directional changes in velocity through the motorized rear wheels of FALL-E. We characterize the resulting stabilizing responses in able-bodied individuals at low risk of falls. Our findings show that changes in step length and anterior-posterior margin of stability (AP MOS) consistently aligned with the direction of the perturbation. In addition, assisted walking with FALL-E elicited distinct biomechanical adaptations not seen in unassisted conditions, including modifications in elbow flexion and trunk flexion. These results provide new insight into balance control strategies during perturbed, device-assisted walking.

items.title: Designers’ Views on Behaviorism, Dependency Concerns and Ethics in Gamification
items.abstract: Gamification is increasingly employed to enhance user engagement, yet these interventions may risk promoting psychological dependency and, depending on their specific design and context, undermining intrinsic motivation. This exploratory study aims to investigate how designers conceptualize behaviorist design principles and navigate the resulting ethical tensions. Employing Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis to investigate the lived experiences of 12 UI/UX designers and design students, the analysis highlights three central themes: participants’ retrospective accounts of shifting from an aesthetic-driven to a behavior-focused design orientation, the navigation of an experienced ethical vacuum, and a perceived deficiency in formal industry guidelines. These insights point to the potential value of developing shared design principles to support more responsible gamification practices, though further research is needed before such principles could inform formal industry standards.

items.title: Designing Trust in AI-Assisted Fashion Education
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming fashion design education by enabling users to produce visually convincing garments, campaign images, and videos with unprecedented speed. However, as the visual quality of AI-assisted outputs becomes increasingly independent of the depth of human-led design reasoning, final outcomes become less reliable as evidence of student learning, authorship, and disciplinary judgment. This article examines this problem through a reflective practice-based case. An educator-led fashion project was documented from initial asset development to AI generation, redesign and market-ready visualization. The analysis reveals several critical tensions, including the limited perceptibility of the designer–system ratio, the limited visibility of the connection between visual research and print development, the mixed sources of the uploaded assets, and the risk that repeated generation and visual selection may replace deliberate design reasoning. The article introduces the concept of the “output–evidence gap” to describe the disconnection between the apparent quality of AI-assisted outcomes and the evidence they provide of authorship, learning, and critical judgment. It subsequently proposes a Designing Trust Framework structured around framing, sourcing, translating, curating, generating, diagnosing, intervening, and accounting. The article argues that trust in AI-assisted design education cannot be based on visual polish or platform-declared human control alone. Instead, it should be built through trackable processes, domain-specific judgment, meaningful human intervention, and deliberate pedagogical mediation.

items.title: Designing Trustworthy AI Systems for Modeling Critical Minerals Recovery Processes
items.abstract: As AI assistance lowers the barrier to coding, domain experts with limited programming experience are increasingly engaging with scientific computing software. However, a critical gap persists: evaluating and trusting AI-generated code remains a significant challenge for verification and validation. Drawing on our experience building the Process Optimization and Modeling for Minerals Sustainability (PrOMMiS) Flowsheet Inspector, a domain-specific tool for code-driven computational software, this poster details our methodology for building user trust. We demonstrate how we enable AI agents and design intuitive UX features to confidently integrate AI assistance into complex computational workflows. PrOMMiS allows chemical engineers to model critical minerals recovery, but the reliance on programmatic Python frameworks slows down setup and troubleshooting for non-programmers. We illustrate specific features within the PrOMMiS UI that directly address this: enabling users to validate AI-driven changes, improve diagnostic accessibility, and enhance error discoverability through an intuitive interface.

items.title: Detecting the Human in the Machine: A Forensic Linguistic Approach to Distinguishing Human, AI, and Hybrid Authorship in Turkish
items.abstract: The proliferation of large language models capable of producing fluent Turkish prose confronts linguistic scholarship with a problem inverse to its longstanding concern: rather than analysing texts of known human provenance, scholars now face the task of determining whether a given text was authored by a human writer, generated by a machine, or composed through some combination of the two. Existing detection systems based on perplexity and burstiness suffer from opacity, English-language bias, and an inability to handle hybrid composition. The present study advances a forensic linguistic alternative grounded in the presence/absence coding framework and Jaccard similarity coefficient developed by Grant (2013) and adapted to Turkish in Kocagül (2022). Drawing on a corpus of 336 argumentative texts produced by 56 participants across six task conditions, the analysis applies 61 active linguistic features distributed across lexical, syntactic, structural, AI-specific, and data-driven categories. Three findings emerge. AI-generated Turkish texts exhibit a coherent feature profile, most distinctively elevated semicolon and comma density, sentence-initial discourse markers, recurrent ‑Arak converb chaining, and formulaic closing vocabulary. The within-author Jaccard baseline (0.41) substantially exceeds all human-to-machine comparisons (0.22-0.30), while the AI-to-hybrid pairing reaches 0.52, confirming the persistence of the AI lexical profile across editorial intervention. In edited hybrid texts, 41 of 61 features (67%) remain shifted from the writers’ baseline toward the AI baseline, indicating that lexical and discourse-organisational features pass below the editor’s threshold of attention. The findings characterise an AI-typical linguistic profile in argumentative Turkish and contribute a Turkish-language case to a corpus linguistic and forensic literature whose principal benchmarks have until recently excluded the language.

items.title: Detection of code smells using artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Introduction: This article is the product of research on code smells developed by the Software Engineering for Education Research Group at the Autonomous University of Yucatán in 2025. This study, like others cited in the literature, has relied on artificial intelligence to expand research in Software Engineering. Problem: Although previous studies have analyzed code smell detection using Machine Learning and Deep Learning independently, this research integrates both approaches to provide a more detailed analysis. Objective: The objective of this study is to present the approach taken toward artificial intelligence and code smells. Method: A systematic mapping study was employed as the research method. Based on a search string executed in five databases—ACM, Taylor & Francis, IEEE, Wiley, and SpringerLink—108 documents were retrieved, of which 35 were selected according to the established inclusion and exclusion criteria. Results: Since 2018, a growing trend in this topic has been observed. Machine Learning is the predominant approach, mainly using the Random Forest algorithm, while CNN stands out in Deep Learning. Conclusion: Despite their growing relevance, there are significant areas that require further attention and research. Originality: This research integrates Machine Learning and Deep Learning approaches within the same study for code smell detection, allowing for a broader view and a more detailed comparison. Limitations: The limitation of this study lies in the fact that the review was based only on five databases and on the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

items.title: DEVELOPING CRITICAL AI LITERACY AMONG FUTURE ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS: EVIDENCE FROM AN EFL TEACHER-EDUCATION CONTEXT
items.abstract: The growing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education has created new opportunities for language learning while raising important questions about the reliability, pedagogical appropriateness, and ethical implications of AI-generated content. In this context, developing critical AI literacy among future English language teachers has become an important objective of contemporary teacher education. This article examines the conceptual foundations and pedagogical dimensions of critical AI literacy, with particular attention to the preparation of prospective EFL teachers. The study employs a qualitative conceptual-analytical approach, drawing on established research on AI literacy, digital competence, technological pedagogical content knowledge, and international AI competency frameworks. The analysis identifies five interconnected dimensions of critical AI literacy: understanding AI systems, evaluating generated information, making pedagogically informed decisions, recognizing ethical risks, and reflecting on AI-supported teaching practices. It further proposes a practice-oriented framework that integrates critical evaluation, lesson design, classroom application, and reflective assessment into EFL teacher education. The article argues that effective AI literacy development requires a shift from operational familiarity with digital tools towards informed, independent, and responsible professional judgment. The proposed framework provides a theoretical basis for curriculum development and future empirical investigation. Since the present study does not include primary data collected from prospective teachers, the framework requires validation through classroom-based research.

items.title: Development and Validation of a Guided Inquiry-Based E-Module Integrating Joyful Learning for Seventh-Grade Science Education
items.abstract: Background. Indonesian students' limited scientific literacy highlights the need for innovative digital learning materials that promote active, engaging, and meaningful science learning. Aims. This study aimed to identify teachers’ and students’ needs, develop a joyful learning e-module integrated with guided Inquiry-Based Learning (IBL), and evaluate its feasibility and practicality for seventh-grade science learning. Methods. The 4D model—define, design, develop, and disseminate—formed the basis of the study's Research and Development (R&D) methodology, which limited the development process to the develop stage. SMPN 2 Krui seventh-grade students, a science teacher, a media specialist, and a material expert participated in the study. The study used descriptive quantitative and qualitative methods to examine data gathered through expert validation sheets, student response surveys, and interviews. The needs analysis showed a need for digital teaching resources that are accessible, interesting, and interactive. Validation data show that the e-module received a feasibility score of 91.08% from the material expert, 86.56% from the media expert, and 100% from the scientific instructor. With an average score of 90.67% for the e-module and 97.94% for the combination of guided IBL and joyful learning, student responses were likewise very favorable. Result. These findings indicate that the developed e-module is highly feasible, practical, and well accepted by students as a digital resource for supporting active and enjoyable science learning. Conclusion. Integrating guided inquiry activities with joyful learning offers a promising approach to combining cognitive engagement with positive learning experiences. Implementation. Further research using larger samples and experimental designs is recommended to examine its effectiveness in improving scientific literacy, critical thinking, and learning outcomes.

items.title: Development of large language model-generated multiple-choice questions and flashcards to enhance the Canadian undergraduate urology curriculum
items.abstract: Introduction: The Canadian Undergraduate Urology Curriculum (CanUUC) is a free, online curriculum that covers important topics in urology for medical students. While multiple-choice questions (MCQs) and flashcards are widely used for medical education, they can be resource-intensive and time-consuming to produce. Therefore, to strengthen the CanUUC with such tools, we developed a customized large language model (LLM)-enabled system to generate MCQs and flashcards from CanUUC material and evaluated the quality of its outputs. Methods: We used OpenAI’s GPT-5 model and refined two system prompts to generate educational materials from two CanUUC topics (benign prostatic hyperplasia and urolithiasis). Six evaluators blinded to items’ origin were involved, and each item received two independent ratings for relevance, correctness, clarity, distractor quality, and suitability for education. Items with a mean score <3 on the suitability for education evaluation domain were excluded. Results were summarized descriptively. Results: Ninety items, including 40 MCQs and 50 flashcards were generated. Among flashcards, 22% allowed >1 plausible answer. Across all independent ratings, the proportion of top scores (4–5) ranged from 85.5−90.5% across all domains. Overall, 86.1% of independent ratings judged items suitable for medical education. When averaging the suitability score at the item-level, 12 items (13%) had a score <3 and were excluded. Mandatory (8%) and optional (27%) adjustments were suggested to refine items’ clarity and correctness. From the initially generated items, 87% were included in the CanUUC. Conclusions: Our customized system can produce curriculum-aligned MCQs and flashcards that meet item writing standards and are mostly suitable for medical education. Expert review is essential to identify flaws and improve quality before inclusion into the curriculum.

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Two Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Systems Versus Dental Students in Endodontic Radiographic Classification
items.abstract: Objectives: Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly used to support image interpretation in dentistry, but evidence regarding their diagnostic performance on endodontic radiographs remains limited. This study compared the diagnostic accuracy of two general-purpose multimodal AI systems with that of undergraduate and postgraduate dental students and evaluated whether image cropping influenced AI performance. Methods: Fifty anonymized periapical radiographs were retrospectively selected, with 10 cases in each of five predefined endodontic diagnostic categories. Reference diagnoses were established by consensus between two experienced endodontists. ChatGPT version 5.2 and Gemini version 3 independently classified each case using both full-size and tooth-cropped images and a standardized prompt. Twenty-five fifth-year undergraduate dental students and 20 postgraduate students in clinical endodontics classified the full-size images. Overall and category-specific accuracies were calculated, and agreement with the reference standard was assessed. Results: Overall accuracy was highest among postgraduate students (84.9%), followed by undergraduate students (78.7%). Gemini achieved accuracies of 72.0% with full-size images and 82.0% with cropped images, whereas ChatGPT achieved 68.0% and 50.0%, respectively. Cropping significantly reduced ChatGPT accuracy (p = 0.0117) but did not significantly affect Gemini performance (p = 0.3018). Diagnostic accuracy varied substantially across categories. Agreement with the reference standard for the AI systems ranged from 50.0% to 82.0%. Conclusions: Diagnostic performance depended on the evaluator, AI system, image format, and diagnostic category. Postgraduate students showed the highest overall accuracy, while AI performance was heterogeneous and did not consistently exceed that of trained human observers. General-purpose multimodal AI may support supervised radiographic interpretation and education, but it should not replace comprehensive clinical assessment or professional judgment.

items.title: Differential-fusion YOLO for MB2 canal detection and recognition in cone-beam computed tomographic images
items.abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based system, called Differential-Fusion YOLO (DF-YOLO), for MB2 canal detection and recognition in cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. DF-YOLO is a dual-branch convolutional architecture that integrates differential feature extraction with adaptive fusion to highlight subtle anatomical variations between adjacent slices. A clinical CBCT dataset comprising 148 microscopically confirmed MB2-positive cases (7,804 axial slices) was retrospectively collected and divided into training ( n = 116), validation ( n = 16), and test ( n = 16) groups. Although all included patients had clinically confirmed MB2 canals, only a limited number of slices from each case contained visible MB2 canal structures; the remaining slices were therefore classified as slice-level negative samples. Model performance was benchmarked against state-of-the-art detectors and further examined through ablation and human–AI comparison studies. For the human–AI comparison, 20 microscopically confirmed MB2-positive cases were included. In addition, an exploratory patient-level analysis was conducted using the 16 MB2-positive cases from the test set and 10 additional MB2-negative cases. DF-YOLO yielded an internal slice-level precision of 83.6%, recall of 87.4%, mAP@0.5 of 92.0%, and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 53.6%. In the exploratory patient-level analysis based on the positive-slice ratio, the model achieved an AUC of 0.881. Using a threshold of ≥ 0.20, the patient-level sensitivity was 93.8%, specificity 60.0%, accuracy 80.8%, positive predictive value (PPV) 78.9%, negative predictive value (NPV) 85.7%, and F1-score 85.7%. In the exploratory human–AI comparison, DF-YOLO achieved higher recall and faster inference than manual slice-level annotation. However, the limited number of positive cases in the clinician reader dataset precludes general conclusions about its diagnostic performance in routine clinical practice. The proposed DF-YOLO approach showed promising internal performance for MB2 canal detection on CBCT ROI slices. The exploratory patient-level analysis showed high sensitivity but only modest specificity in a small supplemental MB2-negative cohort. Larger, more rigorously curated negative-case datasets, external validation, and clinically representative cohorts are needed before clinical implementation can be considered.

items.title: Digital Payment Security and Fraud Prevention in Peer to Peer Payment Systems
items.abstract: The rapid growth of Peer-to-Peer (P2P) payment systems has transformed digital transactions by improving accessibility, speed, and convenience. However, increasing exposure to cyberattacks, unauthorized access, data breaches, and fraudulent transactions raises significant concerns regarding transaction integrity, data confidentiality, and user trust. These challenges highlight the need for comprehensive security frameworks that address evolving threats while maintaining operational efficiency. This study aims to critically evaluate the effectiveness of security protocols and fraud prevention mechanisms in P2P payment systems, focusing on encryption, authentication, tokenization, transaction verification, and real-time fraud detection. A qualitative analytical approach was employed through a systematic review of academic literature, industry reports, and relevant security standards, complemented by a comparative analysis of security implementations across selected P2P payment platforms. The analysis examined security capabilities, fraud mitigation strategies, implementation challenges, and differences in technological and regulatory approaches. The findings indicate that multilayered security architectures combining cryptographic encryption, multifactor authentication, tokenization, and real-time monitoring provide complementary protection against unauthorized transactions and data compromise. However, variations in implementation, system scalability, operational complexity, and regulatory compliance influence overall security effectiveness. The analysis also highlights the importance of balancing robust protection with seamless user experiences. Effective P2P payment security requires integrated, adaptive, and continuously updated security frameworks supported by consistent risk assessment and regulatory alignment. Future research should investigate artificial intelligence-driven fraud detection, blockchain-enabled transaction verification, and adaptive authentication to strengthen resilience against emerging threats while preserving user trust and sustainable platform development.

items.title: Digital tools for financial transparency: Challenges, opportunities and prospects
items.abstract: Financial transparency has become a major issue in an increasingly globalized and digitized world. Our work explores the role of digital tools in improving financial transparency, a crucial challenge for companies, governments, and financial institutions. Through a literature review and case studies, our work examines technologies such as blockchain, artificial intelligence (AI), open data platforms (Open Data), and cloud computing. These tools enhance the integrity, traceability, and accessibility of financial data, while reducing the risk of fraud and corruption. For example, blockchain guarantees secure, immutable transactions, while AI detects anomalies and automates auditing processes. Results show that the adoption of these technologies improves corporate governance, boosts stakeholder confidence and facilitates the management of public finances. However, challenges remain, notably in terms of cost, technical skills and data protection. Our work offers recommendations for overcoming these obstacles, such as employee training, regulatory oversight and the promotion of international standards. Digital tools represent a major opportunity to transform financial transparency, provided they are deployed thoughtfully and inclusively. Their adoption could contribute to a more equitable and sustainable management of financial resources, while strengthening trust in economic and political systems.

items.title: Digital Transformation in Language Teaching: From Traditional Methods to Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: This article examines the digital transformation of language teaching and analyses the impact of contemporary digital technologies and artificial intelligence on the language-teaching process. It focuses on the evolution of traditional forms of instruction, the potential of digital educational technologies, and the main areas where artificial intelligence is applied in language teaching. The advantages of using intelligent systems are examined, including the personalisation of instruction, the automation of instructional guidance, increased access to educational resources, and opportunities for online learning. The article identifies the main risks to academic integrity. It addresses issues of information reliability, the protection of learners’ personal data, and the preservation of the teacher’s leading role in the educational process. Contemporary scholarly works related to the subject have been examined. Based of an analysis of the theoretical literature on the issues under investigation, the article demonstrates the need of integrate artificial intelligence technologies harmoniously into language education while preserving education’s humanistic orientation of education and recognising the importance of the teacher’s role as a mentor and facilitator. It is concluded that the most promising model for the development of contemporary language education is one based on collaboration between the teacher and artificial intelligence. Such a model contributes to improving the quality of instruction, developing communicative competence, saving time and human resources, and fostering learners’ digital skills.

items.title: Dishonorable Machines: Why and How to Resist Trial by AI Judges
items.abstract: Just as humans trust human doctors to treat human ills, we trust human judges to resolve human disputes. A doctor may employ artificial intelligence (AI) tools to aid in diagnosis, but the doctor ultimately decides what to prescribe, and the doctor bears accountability for that choice. This Article argues that judging demands the same boundary: AI may assist as a tool, but it must not replace human decision-making. Perhaps unsurprisingly, in light of AI’s recent gains in its ability to process large quantities of seemingly complex material, some scholars and practitioners have contended otherwise, urging that at least some judging be handed off to AI entirely. This Article argues against that call. First, there are many reasons to resist any delegation of judicial power to AI, chiefly that the process of determining the “right answer” to a novel legal question is inherently a human one. That is, even if an AI model arrives at a credited “right answer” much of the time, that result is not what makes the answer correct in the first place. Moreover, constitutional and empirical concerns weigh against AI adjudication. Second, drawing on the comprehensive statutory regime governing federal magistrate judges, there are at least three important constraints that we can and should impose upon the courts’ use of AI: Such use should be consistent with well-informed legislation or regulation, it must be meaningfully transparent, and there must be de novo review by an Article III judge over any AI determination.

items.title: Do College Students Prefer AI Health Coaches Over Human Health Coaches? – A Mix-Method Exploratory Study
items.abstract: Background Rising rates of chronic disease, mental health concerns, and lifestyle-related challenges among college students highlight the need for scalable approaches to support student well-being.Purpose This study developed and tested the feasibility of an artificial intelligence (AI) virtual health coach and compared it to human coaches among college students.Methods Thirty-one college students completed six coaching sessions with seven trained human coaches and two consecutive sessions with an AI coach. The AI agent was developed using prompt engineering on a commercial large language model platform. After each session, students completed quantitative evaluations. Semi-structured interviews were conducted.Results Students rated human coaching sessions significantly higher than AI sessions across all evaluated dimensions. Rater evaluations indicated comparable performance between AI and human coaches, but human coaches demonstrated significantly greater empathy and helpfulness. Qualitative findings revealed that human coaches were valued for care, connection, accountability, and responsiveness, whereas AI coaches were perceived as nonjudgmental, accessible, and highly structured, with strengths in goal clarification and information delivery.Discussion Whereas human coaches were preferred overall, AI health coaching demonstrated feasibility and potential value as a complementary, scalable support tool.Transition to Health Education Practice Practitioners should proactively seek training in AI tools, prompt design, and safety-tuning so they can effectively and responsibly deploy AI as a supplemental tool for the health coaching practice.

items.title: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
items.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answer. We evaluate four systems (a single-LLM baseline and three multi-agent topologies) across four models and three clinical tasks, scoring hallucination, under a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, inside the rationale each system generates and reporting it alongside the task metric. We report that collaboration buys task performance but not lower hallucination as a rule, and no topology is reliably better than another. The effect differs by model: of the $36$ model--system--task comparisons, $12$ are large enough to resolve --- four decreases and eight increases, with no model on both sides. What sets the level, and the direction of any change, is the model rather than the topology or the number of agents. A self-correction experiment is consistent with this: shown its own flagged errors, every model except Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct reduces hallucination; the one model for which collaboration lowers hallucination gains the most, and Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, the model whose hallucination it amplifies most, does not reduce its hallucination at all. We find that collaboration redistributes what its models can already do; it does not supply what they cannot.

items.title: Does Private Equity Hurt or Improve Healthcare Value? New Evidence and Mechanisms
items.abstract: What is the impact of private equity (PE) ownership on healthcare value? Does PE ownership reduce healthcare value, and if so, can its effect be mitigated using health information technologies (IT)? Given the significant investments by PE firms in the healthcare sector in recent years, it is increasingly important for stakeholders, including policy makers, care providers, and patients, to understand their likely impact and whether PE ownership is aligned with their interests. Because PE firms seek to improve efficiency and generate short-term financial returns, the cost-cutting strategies used to achieve these goals may come at the expense of care quality, leading to competing hypotheses on the impact of PE ownership on healthcare value. We argue that IT-enabled health information sharing capabilities can help PE-owned hospitals to better manage this cost-quality tension and achieve higher healthcare value. Using a staggered difference-in-differences approach and data from US hospitals from 2008 to 2020, we estimate changes in healthcare value following PE acquisition and ownership. Overall, we find that PE ownership of hospitals reduces healthcare value. This decline is partially driven by reduction in clinical staffing following PE ownership. We further find that pre-existing, hospital health information sharing capabilities mitigate the negative impact of PE ownership on healthcare value. Specifically, such capabilities can strengthen the effect of PE ownership on cost reduction and, at the same time, mitigate PE-induced, care quality deterioration. Our results highlight the critical role of common data standards needed to promote IT-enabled information sharing between healthcare providers, which, in turn, can align the incentives of PE firms with the goals of value-based care.

items.title: DStill: Trajectory Consistency Distillation for Accelerated One-Step Drafting in Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
items.abstract: Block-diffusion speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by drafting multiple tokens in parallel. However, one-step drafting in discrete diffusion is limited by token factorization error: each token is predicted from the same masked block, without conditioning on the tokens selected at other positions in that step. This can produce inconsistent drafts and reduce acceptance length. Iterative refinement mitigates this limitation by conditioning later predictions on previously committed tokens, though additional passes increase drafting cost. To address this trade-off between draft fidelity and inference latency, we introduce DStill, a two-stage framework that distills a target-conditioned drafter's own multi-step refinement into one-step drafting. We first train the drafter to complete partially revealed blocks, then use its refinement trajectories to train a student to predict the final completion in one pass. Using a curriculum that gradually transitions from partial to fully masked inputs, we successfully transfer the multi-step refinement capabilities into one step. Across reasoning, math, code benchmarks on three model families DStill improves acceptance length by up to 28% and speedup by up to 25% over one-step DFlash, achieving up to 6.45x speedup over auto-regressive decoding.

items.title: Early and visible detection of fugitive methane leaks in industrial infrared videos via local-global contrast enhancement
items.abstract: Early visualization of greenhouse gases and volatile organic compounds is essential for emission control and industrial safety. Infrared optical gas imaging sequences are difficult to interpret because plumes occupy little of each frame. In our data, mean plume coverage was 6.12%, mean local contrast was 8.09%, and over 72% of samples had local contrast below 10%. We develop an artificial intelligence framework for infrared methane-plume enhancement and early leak detection. It embeds a Local Perception Enhancement Module in a U-shaped Transformer and combines differentiable local contrast limiting, spatial gating, and residual fusion. The study used 180,000 infrared frames from controlled releases and an operating chemical industrial park. The framework achieved a region-of-interest peak signal-to-noise ratio of 35.41 dB and a global structural similarity index of 0.951. Structural ablation confirmed gains in local and global fidelity, structural similarity, and contrast. With a fixed one-stage object detector, enhanced inputs increased mean intersection over union from 76% to 85% and reduced false negatives by 31.5%. For controlled releases of 80 to 4000 mL per minute, enhancement lowered the flow rate at which probability of detection reached 0.9 from 1000 to 300 mL per minute. At two field sites, stable detection occurred 10.5 and 11.8 s earlier. These results connect artificial intelligence-based image enhancement to measurable gains in industrial methane-leak monitoring.

items.title: Early Exposure to Artificial Intelligence in Medical Education: A Knowledge, Attitude and Practice Study among Preclinical Medical Students from Mangaluru, India
items.abstract: Introduction: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the study of machines that learn from collected data and use human-like reasoning. AI applications are already used in healthcare, and there is a need to understand the need for AI training in the medical curriculum. Aim: To assess the Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) related to AI among first- and second-year MBBS students. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at AJ Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Centre, Mangaluru, Karnataka, India from April to May 2026, among first- and second-year MBBS students via an online questionnaire; the sample size was 327. Based on existing KAP studies, the questionnaire collected data on AI knowledge (e.g., AI/ML concepts and applications), attitudes (e.g., beliefs about fostering AI knowledge despite its future application), and AI application. Categorical associations were analysed using Chisquare tests. Statistical significance was set at p-value <0.05. Results: Of 327 survey participants, 204 (62.39%) were firstyear medical students. Most reported at least basic knowledge of AI; however, few had prior training {26 (7.95%) attended AI workshops, and 41 (12.54%) received curriculum training}. Most students believed medical schools should teach AI concepts (269, 82.26%) and supported incorporating AI into the curriculum (193, 59.02%). ChatGPT was the most popular AI tool, used by 315 (96.33%) respondents, primarily for exam preparation and studying, with other uses less frequent. The key obstacles included insufficient knowledge/lack of proper training in AI (222, 67.89%) and concerns about data privacy and ethical issues (157,48.01%). Conclusion: Despite extensive exposure to AI (as most students used AI tools), students had limited knowledge or training in it. Students were optimistic about AI in healthcare and strongly supported AI education. These results suggest incorporating AI training into the medical curriculum to bridge knowledge gaps and meet learners’ needs.

items.title: Economic Turbulence and Organizational AI Use in MSMEs: The Competing Roles of Perceived Benefits and Risks
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) may support adaptation in micro-, small-, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) facing economic uncertainty. This study examines a dual-pathway appraisal framework using a cross-sectional survey of 537 respondents reporting on Chinese MSMEs already using AI. The outcome represents the extent of organizational AI use rather than initial adoption or continuance intention. Confirmatory factor analysis and latent-variable structural equation modeling were conducted with 5000 case-bootstrap resamples. The specification adds familiarity–appraisal paths and a benefit–risk residual covariance. Economic turbulence was positively associated with perceived benefits, which were positively associated with AI use. The specific indirect association through benefits was significant (B = 0.058, 95% CI [0.013, 0.118]), whereas the risk-mediated association was not. Perceived risks were negatively associated with AI use. Familiarity was positively associated with use and risks, but its association with benefits was nonsignificant. The direct turbulence–use association was nonsignificant; the total association was positive and significant (B = 0.209, 95% CI [0.047, 0.371]). items.title: Effect of a Health Education Program on the Prevention of Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders on School Teachers’ Knowledge
items.abstract: Background: Physical and occupational demands of teachers due to their profession exposed them various ergonomic risk factors, making them particularly vulnerable to musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs).This study assessed the effect of a health education program on the prevention of work-related musculoskeletal disorders on school teachers' knowledge.Method: A quasi-experimental study using a one-group pre-and post-test design was implemented at four primary institutes located within the El Mansoura Azharian Zone.A total of 46 school teachers agreed to participate in the study.Three data collection tools were used: a socio-demographic and occupational data self-administered questionnaire, a school teachers' knowledge self-administered questionnaire, and teachers' feedback related to the educational program implementation.Results: Reported significant improvements with a large effect size (t=23.88,P≤0.001, d=4.79) in the teachers' knowledge of work-related musculoskeletal disorders, including definitions, types, signs and symptoms, ergonomics, and management from the pre-test to the post-test assessment of the educational program Conclusion and Recommendations: The study found that the work-related musculoskeletal disorders program effectively increased teachers' knowledge regarding musculoskeletal disorders and ergonomics.The study recommends continuing to provide interventions such as occupational health education lectures, on-site ergonomics training, and publicity brochures to enhance teachers' health knowledge regarding work-related musculoskeletal disorders.

items.title: EFL LEARNERS' PERCEPTIONS OF AI TOOLS FOR SPEAKING PRACTICE AND SPEAKING ANXIETY: A PROPOSED SURVEY OF FIRST-YEAR UNIVERSITY STUDENTS IN UZBEKISTAN
items.abstract: This proposed study aims to explore first-year university EFL learners' perceptions of using artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as conversational AI assistants and pronunciation applications, for English-speaking practice. It focuses on learners' perceived speaking anxiety, perceived usefulness of feedback, and views about the advantages and limitations of AI-supported practice. A questionnaire-based survey is planned with approximately 30 first-year students studying English Language and Literature at Andijan State Institute of Foreign Languages. The questionnaire will include Likert-scale items and a small number of open-ended questions. Quantitative responses will be summarized using descriptive statistics, while open-ended responses will be grouped into recurring themes. Because data have not yet been collected, this proposal does not report empirical findings or claim that AI tools improve speaking performance. The study is intended to provide context-specific preliminary evidence about how students perceive AI-assisted speaking practice and to inform future, larger-scale research.
